title: Research
text: My research focuses on microbial water quality and the use of data-driven approaches to better understand, monitor, and predict changes in aquatic and drinking water systems.

title: Research
text:
Online microbial water quality monitoring
I work with online and high-frequency monitoring approaches, particularly flow cytometry, to characterize microbial communities and detect changes in microbial water quality.

title: Research
text:
Data science & machine learning
I apply machine learning and statistical methods to complex water quality datasets, including anomaly detection, explainable AI, and time-series forecasting. My research aims to develop approaches that are both scientifically interpretable and practically useful.

title: Research
section: Environmental drivers of microbial water quality
text:
Environmental drivers of microbial water quality
I investigate how environmental and hydrometeorological conditions influence microbial water quality. By combining microbial measurements with environmental data, I aim to better understand the processes driving short-term changes in water quality.

title: Research
text:
From research to practice
As an industrial PhD researcher, an important part of my work is translating research into approaches that can support water utilities in monitoring and managing water quality.

title: Isabel K. Erb
text:
PhD Researcher in Microbial Water Quality & Data Science
I am an industrial PhD researcher at Lund University and Sweden Water Research. My research focuses on microbial water quality monitoring and the application of data-driven methods to better understand and predict changes in water quality.
My work combines online monitoring, flow cytometry, environmental data, and machine learning, with a particular interest in translating these approaches into practical tools for water utilities.

title: About
text:
I am an industrial PhD researcher at Lund University and Sweden Water Research, working at the intersection of microbial water quality, environmental monitoring, and data science.
My research explores how high-frequency microbial and environmental data can be used to better understand changes in water quality. I am particularly interested in online flow cytometry, machine learning, explainable AI, anomaly detection, and predictive modelling.
Through my industrial PhD, I work closely with the water sector, with the aim of connecting methodological research with practical challenges in water quality monitoring and management.

title: Curriculum Vitae
text:
Profile
Final-year industrial PhD candidate in Biotechnology and Applied Microbiology, specializing in data-driven monitoring of microbial water quality. My research combines online flow cytometry, automated E. coli measurements, environmental fieldwork, and explainable machine learning to study microbial water quality in urban coastal, bathing-water, groundwater, and drinking-water systems.
I develop interpretable forecasting and anomaly-detection methods in collaboration with water utilities in Sweden and Iceland.

title: Curriculum Vitae
text:
Research Experience

Doctoral Student
Lund University and Sweden Water Research AB, Sweden
October 2022–present

Implement and evaluate automated monitoring procedures integrating online flow cytometry, enzymatic E. coli measurements, and environmental data.
Develop Python-based classification and forecasting models for fecal indicator bacteria in urban waters.
Develop baseline-free anomaly-detection pipelines using unsupervised machine learning.
Apply SHAP to investigate microbial anomalies in relation to operational and meteorological conditions.
Conduct culture-based and phenotypic analyses of environmental E. coli.



Visiting Doctoral Researcher
Veitur, Reykjavík, Iceland
March–May 2025

Conducted automated monitoring of groundwater used for drinking-water production using online flow cytometry.
Applied unsupervised machine learning to identify anomalous changes in groundwater microbial communities.
Evaluated detected anomalies using utility operational records and meteorological data.
Used explainable AI to identify the flow cytometric features associated with microbial anomalies.



Research Assistant
Sweden Water Research, Lund, Sweden
June–October 2022

Established continuous microbial monitoring of seawater using a BactoSense online flow cytometer and a ColiMinder enzymatic E. coli monitor.
Monitored instrument performance and data quality during field deployment.
Processed and analyzed microbial and environmental monitoring data.



Master’s Thesis Student
Lund University, Sweden
January–June 2022

Analyzed whole-genome sequences of environmental E. coli isolated from marine sediments.
Characterized halotolerance, antibiotic susceptibility, and biofilm formation.
Performed statistical analyses of genomic and phenotypic characteristics.

title: Curriculum Vitae
text:
Selected Skills

Flow cytometry: Conventional, automated, and online systems; 2D fingerprint analysis
Scientific computing: Python, pandas, scikit-learn, R, and QGIS
Machine learning: Random Forest, Isolation Forest, support vector machines, logistic regression, and LSTM
Time-series analysis and explainable AI: Forecasting, anomaly detection, and SHAP
Molecular microbiology: DNA extraction, quantification, and whole-genome sequencing preparation
Bioinformatics: SKESA, CheckM, RGI, ClermonTyping, and MLST
Phenotypic assays: Antibiotic susceptibility, growth, halotolerance, UV inhibition, and biofilm formation
Environmental fieldwork: Water, sediment, soil, and air sampling
Research practice: Experimental design, statistical analysis, scientific writing, and student mentoring
